sample_unit: external test chest radiographs read by 3 junior residents with and without AI
models_evaluated: deep neural network three-class CXR classifier (non-pneumonia, non-COVID-19 pneumonia, COVID-19 pneumonia)

links.outcome: Junior resident diagnostic performance with versus without AI assistance on external CXRs
links.effect: Residents' performance improved inversely to training level with AI assistance; two of three junior residents showed significant improvement.
links.quote: Among the three junior residents, two showed significant improvement with the assistance of AI.

links.outcome: Model performance drop from internal to external test set (domain shift)
links.effect: AUC 0.9518 on internal test set versus 0.8594 on external test set; authors suggest domain shift between datasets.
links.quote: This suggests a domain shift between the patient dataset and the external dataset, highlighting the need for future research on test-time training domain adaptation to address this issue.

screen.reason: The study conducts a multireader offline study evaluating the impact of AI assistance versus unassisted reading on the diagnostic accuracy of junior residents interpreting chest radiographs.
